proposed.explanation:
Profit attributable to Talaat Moustafa Group's own shareholders (the Parent Company) rose from 9,025,066,065 LE in 2024 (restated) to 14,383,890,306 LE in 2025, an increase of 5,358,824,241 LE or roughly 59.4%. This is corroborated by EPS jumping from 4.38 LE to 6.98 LE (+59.4%), gross profit growing from 14.00 bn to 20.86 bn LE (+48.9%), and pre-tax profit rising from 16.49 bn to 23.65 bn LE (+43.4%). Total equity also expanded by about 21.4% to 157.71 bn LE, indicating the profit is being retained and building the balance sheet rather than being fully paid out.

For a 5-10-year growth investor with high loss tolerance, a ~59% jump in parent-shareholder profit in a single year is a strong positive signal and supports keeping the existing 500-share position. However, I cannot recommend buying more TMGH: your portfolio is 71,250 EGP (30,000 cash + 500 × 82.50 = 41,250 in TMGH), so TMGH already represents 57.9% of total value. The diversification rule caps any single holding at 50% after a buy, and because the current weight already exceeds that ceiling, no additional TMGH purchase is permissible. You would need to either sell some TMGH or add a different company before the cap could be met.

Risks and caveats: (1) The 2024 column is labelled 'Restated,' so part of the apparent growth may reflect accounting reclassifications rather than purely organic improvement. (2) We have only a single year-over-year comparison; one strong year does not guarantee a sustained 5-10-year trend. (3) No revenue, cash-flow, debt, or sector-level data are provided, so the quality and durability of the profit growth cannot be fully assessed. (4) The share price of 82.50 EGP implies a P/E of roughly 11.8× on 2025 EPS of 6.98 LE, which is not obviously expensive, but valuation context (sector multiples, growth sustainability) is outside the evidence provided. In summary, the fundamentals support holding your current position, but the evidence is insufficient to justify a larger allocation, and the diversification rule independently prevents one.
